name: Financial
summary: Follow-the-money entities: bank accounts with their fraud-report status, and exchanges and other virtual-asset service providers. Public identifiers only — no keys, PANs, or credentials.
description:
Reach for it to trace funds through bank accounts, such as the mule accounts a fraud case pays into, and through exchanges and other virtual-asset service providers. Cryptocurrency addresses and transactions belong to the Cryptocurrency pack, which tells networks apart.

- **Public identifiers only.** No property holds a private key, a card number (PAN) or a credential.
- **Exchanges.** `exchange` is any service that holds customers' funds: an exchange, an OTC desk, a custodial wallet, a payment processor. The Cryptocurrency pack's `crypto_service` is for the ones that do not. One is identified by its name alone, as written, case included.
- **Bank accounts.** One is identified by bank code and account number together: the same number at two banks is two accounts. Write both without spaces or hyphens, and the bank as its code, not its name; an IBAN takes no bank code. One recorded before 2.0.0 has no bank code and does not merge with new writes of it. Fraud registration and payment suspension hold as of `status_checked_at`, and a registration can be released later. The holder of record is often not whoever used the account. Its `currency` is an ISO 4217 code.

**Source:** https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/typepack-basic (`typepacks/financial.json`). Licence: Apache-2.0.

types.name: exchange
types.description: A cryptocurrency exchange or other virtual-asset service provider that holds customers' funds: an exchange, OTC desk, custodial wallet or payment processor.

types.name: bank_account
types.description: A bank account. Identified by (bank_code, account_identifier), because an account number is unique only within its bank. A mule account in a fraud case is this type, with its report status alongside; whoever operated it is an identity.person linked by an edge.

account_identifier.description: Account number without spaces or hyphens (123-456-789012 is written 123456789012), or an IBAN in its electronic form (DE89370400440532013000): digits and capital letters only. Half the account's identity, with bank_code.

bank_code.description: The country's own bank code if it has one (Korea's three digits: 004 KB Kookmin, 088 Shinhan, 090 KakaoBank; a UK sort code; a US routing number), else the SWIFT/BIC (8 or 11 capitals). No spaces or hyphens; never the bank's name. Empty for an IBAN. Half the account's identity.

bank_name.description: Holding bank's name, as shown. Identity uses bank_code, not this.

account_holder.description: Name of the holder of record (Korea: 명의인). Often not who used the account: the holder may have sold or lent it, or had it opened in their name, so whoever operated it is a separate identity.person linked by an edge.

fraud_registration.description: Whether the account is registered as used for fraud: in Korea, a fraud-use account (사기이용계좌) under the Telecommunications Financial Fraud Act. not_registered means checked and not found; released means registered once and since released. As of status_checked_at.

payment_suspended_at.description: When payments from the account were suspended (Korea: 지급정지).

report_channels.description: Where the account was reported, one per line (e.g. 112, 1332 (FSS), the holding bank, ECRM, TheCheat).

status_checked_at.description: When fraud_registration and payment_suspended_at were last confirmed.

status_source.description: Who confirmed them: the holding bank, a police or FSS notice, a lookup service, a victim's report.
